criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no operation whose outcome reaches a domain entrypoint, command handler, formatter or the wire format.

criteria.statement: Callers of a result-returning operation check .ok rather than catching exceptions to learn the outcome.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no caller of a result-returning operation.

criteria.statement: Callers that report a failure to the user render the result .errors and .warnings rather than the text of a caught exception.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no caller that reports a result-returning operation's failure to the user.

criteria.statement: An internal helper that returns a plain value or an error message (str | None) serves a single in-layer caller that only branches on success.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no internal helper that returns a plain value or str | None.

rules.intent: CLI wiring is proven through the real runner, so option binding, exit codes and output cannot silently break. Handler-level tests exist only where the handler owns logic of its own, and never repeat what the domain tests pin.

criteria.statement: Every CLI command action has at least one *CliIntegrationTests suite that invokes the command through runner.invoke.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no CLI command action.

criteria.statement: The integration suite includes a happy-path test with default arguments that asserts exit code 0.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no CLI command action.

criteria.statement: Every declared Typer option, flag and argument of the command is exercised in at least one invocation, verifying input binding and propagation to the domain layer.
criteria.na_when: The command declares no options, flags or arguments.

criteria.statement: The integration suite avoids duplicating domain branch matrices, limiting its binding checks to what the CLI layer adds.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no CLI command action.

criteria.statement: The integration suite includes a failure-path test that asserts the expected non-zero exit code when the domain returns a non-ok result.
criteria.na_when: The command's domain call cannot return a non-ok result.

criteria.statement: The integration suite includes a test invoking the command with --format json that asserts the emitted payload matches the wire schema.
criteria.na_when: The command does not support --format json.

criteria.statement: Every interactive confirmation or abort branch of the command is exercised by the integration suite.
criteria.na_when: The command has no interactive confirmation or abort branch.

criteria.statement: Every *RootTests suite is written for a handler that owns logic the domain layer does not, such as input coercion, branch selection across services, result composition from more than one call, or an interactive abort path.
criteria.na_when: The command action has no *RootTests suite; a pass-through handler with zero root tests is fully compliant and a root test is never required per action.

criteria.statement: Every *RootTests suite avoids restating a contract already asserted under tests/core/ for the same result type.
criteria.na_when: The command action has no *RootTests suite.

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Every CLI command action has at least one *CliIntegrationTests suite that invokes the command through runner.invoke. 2. criteria.na_when: The formatter has no derived view model, meaning transform is provably the identity and the declared view type is the input event type.

criteria.statement: The JSON wire format is asserted as an exact literal dict.

criteria.statement: The JSON wire format is pinned at both a fully populated state and an empty or sparse boundary state.

criteria.statement: A formatter with no derived view model omits the transform test while keeping both the JSON and the render test.
criteria.na_when: The formatter has a derived view model, so transform is not the identity.

criteria.statement: The change is free of an alias such as SomeView = SomeEvent introduced to manufacture a third test for an identity formatter.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no formatter under cli/ui/formatters/.

criteria.statement: The change is free of an assertion that to_json_serializable(data) equals transform(data).model_dump().
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no formatter under cli/ui/formatters/.

rules.name: Parameterization-First for Sibling Variations
rules.intent: Variations of one contract are tested through a single parameterized test, so each case is named and reported separately and a new case costs one line instead of a copied test.

criteria.statement: Variations of the same contract or function (input variants, polymorphic target types, invalid payload permutations) are covered by one parameterized test rather than by copy-pasted or near-identical sibling test methods.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no tests that exercise more than one variation of the same contract.

criteria.statement: Each test is free of `for` loops and stacked assertions that iterate over scenarios.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no tests.

criteria.statement: Every parameterized case uses pytest.param with an explicit, readable id label.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no parameterized tests.

criteria.statement: Separate test methods are used only where the cases have fundamentally distinct lifecycles, differing fixture requirements or divergent assertion contracts.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no tests that sit next to a sibling test of the same function.

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. rules.bad_pattern: def test_eval_model(self): ...; def test_eval_dict(self): ...  # hypothetical: duplicate sibling methods that differ only by target type

rules.name: Assert Domain Invariants on Results; Pin Schemas in Dedicated Contract Tests
rules.intent: Protects tests that fail only when behavior breaks. Assertions target the domain outcome under test, and model shapes and defaults are pinned once in contract tests, so unrelated changes do not break scenario tests.

criteria.statement: Every field assertion in a scenario test checks a field that carries the scenario's domain outcome rather than an incidental envelope field or default.
criteria.na_when: The test is a dedicated model contract test or a wire payload test.

criteria.statement: Each scenario or integration test of a specific behavior or error condition uses targeted field assertions instead of whole-model equality.
criteria.na_when: The test is a wire payload test, or the entire entity is the subject under test (its expected model may then rely on schema defaults instead of naming every field in kwargs).

criteria.statement: Each new or modified model with defaults or a serialization contract has a dedicated contract test in tests/common/ or tests/core/*/test_models.py that asserts them.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no model that has defaults or a serialization contract.

criteria.statement: Model shape, default values and serialization are asserted only in dedicated contract tests rather than in scenario or integration tests.
criteria.na_when: No new or modified scenario or integration test asserts a model's shape, default values or serialization.

criteria.statement: Each model has at most two dedicated contract tests.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or modifies no dedicated model contract test.

criteria.statement: Each test of a wire payload with a published schema contract, such as a CLI JSON formatter, verifies the exact wire payload.
criteria.na_when: No new or modified test covers a wire payload with a published schema contract.

criteria.statement: Each test avoids faux-matchers such as ANY_TIMESTAMP and ANY_UUID where their only purpose is to satisfy whole-object matching on database records or unowned system state.
criteria.na_when: The test uses no faux-matcher.

rules.intent: A test double must stand in for something production really uses, so tests fail when production contracts change instead of passing against an invented interface.

criteria.na_when: The change adds or edits no test double or stub.

criteria.statement: Every test double is free of an interface built as the union of the attributes from every branch of a hasattr chain.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or edits no test double or stub.

rules.intent: Tests prove what the live codebase does, never the historical outcome of a refactor, so a removed symbol leaves no trace in the test suite.

criteria.statement: The test suite is free of negative existence assertions such as assert not hasattr(module, name).

rules.name: Complete Assertions Invariant
rules.intent: A test must check the behavior it exists for, so a passing run shows the code did the right thing and not merely that it returned something.

criteria.statement: Every test checks a concrete value or effect beyond `assert x is not None`, so that `assert x is not None` is never its only assertion.
criteria.na_when: The test contains no assertions on a returned object, for example a test that only checks that a call raises.

criteria.statement: isinstance is used in a test only where it distinguishes two real code paths, rather than repeating what basedpyright already proves.
criteria.na_when: The test uses no isinstance check.

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Every test checks a concrete value or effect beyond `assert x is not None`, so that `assert x is not None` is never its only assertion. 2. isinstance is used in a test only where it distinguishes two real code paths, rather than repeating what basedpyright already proves.

rules.name: Determinism and Clock Virtualization
rules.intent: Tests must give the same result on every run and every machine, so they do not depend on real elapsed time or on leftover processes, and a failing test cannot leak anything into later ones.

criteria.statement: Every test body is free of hardcoded sleeps, other than a sleep inside the shared harness poll helper.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or edits no test code.

criteria.statement: Tests of retry or backoff intervals drive time through VirtualClock or a monkeypatched clock at the module boundary (time.monotonic, asyncio.sleep).
criteria.na_when: The change adds or edits no test of a retry or backoff interval.

criteria.statement: A retry test asserts the resulting schedule rather than only that a retry eventually happened.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or edits no retry test.

criteria.statement: The clock is injected anywhere its output reaches a result field, so a time-dependent test asserts literal timestamps.
criteria.na_when: The code under test has no timestamp that reaches a result field.

criteria.statement: Generated ids are injected anywhere their output reaches a result field, so a test asserts literal ids.
criteria.na_when: The code under test has no generated id that reaches a result field.

criteria.statement: Every wait on an operating system event with no virtual equivalent, such as a process group reaped after SIGKILL, is done through a shared harness helper owning the poll interval and deadline, with no open-coded poll loop.
criteria.na_when: The change waits on no operating system event.

criteria.statement: Every test that spawns a process registers it with the harness process registry, so a failing test cannot leak a process group.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or edits no test that spawns a process.

rules.evaluation_criteria: 1. Every test body is free of hardcoded sleeps, other than a sleep inside the shared harness poll helper. 2. Tests of retry or backoff intervals drive time through VirtualClock or a monkeypatched clock at the module boundary (time.monotonic, asyncio.sleep). 3. A retry test asserts the resulting schedule rather than only that a retry eventually happened. 4. The clock is injected anywhere its output reaches a result field, so a time-dependent test asserts literal timestamps. 5. Generated ids are injected anywhere their output reaches a result field, so a test asserts literal ids. 6. Every wait on an operating system event with no virtual equivalent, such as a process group reaped after SIGKILL, is done through a shared harness helper owning the poll interval and deadline, with no open-coded poll loop. 7. Every test that spawns a process registers it with the harness process registry, so a failing test cannot leak a process group.
rules.bad_pattern: time.sleep(0.05)  # bare sleep in a test body, as in _sync_and_interrupt in tests/engine/executors/test_process_group.py

rules.intent: Code exists to serve real behavior, so nothing stays alive only because a test exercises it. Unused production or harness code is deleted together with its test, not kept and verified.

criteria.statement: Every touched production function has a real caller in src/, so that deleting its tests would not leave it unreachable.

rules.name: Strict Typing on Test Helpers and Fixtures
rules.intent: Test helpers and fixtures are code that every test leans on, so they are typed as tightly as production code and a wrong call is caught by the type checker instead of surfacing as a confusing test failure.

rules.name: Mechanical Enforcement Parity
rules.intent: A BLOCKER rule that can be checked by a machine is actually checked by one, so a declared gate cannot silently stop protecting the codebase and an allowlist cannot quietly grow.

criteria.statement: Every BLOCKER rule that can be checked mechanically has an executing check (an invariant test under tests/lint/, a prek hook or a CI step) or an explicit review-only classification.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or alters no BLOCKER rule and removes no enforcing check.

criteria.statement: Every declared gate is configured so that it can fail, with no setting that disables it, such as a coverage floor of zero or a type checker present in no hook and no workflow.
criteria.na_when: The change touches no gate configuration in prek.toml, .github/workflows/ or pyproject.toml.

criteria.statement: A gate whose configuration disables it is either wired up or downgraded to a review-time WARNING, rather than left declared as an enforced BLOCKER.
criteria.na_when: No declared gate is found to be disabled.

criteria.statement: Every invariant check includes a regression test shaped like the code it polices, such as assertions inside a *Tests class rather than a module-level function.
criteria.na_when: The change adds or alters no invariant check under tests/lint/.

criteria.statement: An invariant check that lands green carries an explicit burn-down allowlist of known violators, rather than being merged red or left disabled.
criteria.na_when: The invariant check lands with no existing violators.

criteria.statement: Every allowlist of known violators has only shrunk, with no entry added.
criteria.na_when: The change touches no allowlist.
